doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

chapter: The Four Seasons and Bob Crewe
title: Writing his first string arrangement
summary: Never having written for strings, he wrote a unison three-violin part for Crewe and was relieved when it sounded great.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: How did you know what strings were capable of? Was that from partly your high school education?

I had no idea. Didn’t have a clue. I mean I studied scores and I saw them. So now this is also interesting. Ariana Grande on the Tonight Show mentioned that – because I recorded her when she was twelve years old and wrote arrangements for her when she was seven with the Pops here in town. But she mentioned on the Tonight Show the first record I ever made with Bob Crewe. She found it and took the song and used it in one of her albums. And she said, “And my grandfather’s best friend, Charlie Calello, and I saw his name on the record.” So there was a little bit of a history behind that record. But now I had to write strings. Now at that point I’d never written for strings. I had only written for horns. And Bob gave me an idea and I also had some knowledge from looking at scores, but I really had no idea how quickly the string players would read it. So I wrote this arrangement and it was only for three violins, and it basically was all in unison. And it had runs in it. And I went to the studio, I was panicked. And I can’t tell you – I kept saying to myself I know this is going to – I can’t believe that it’s going to sound good. I put it in front of them, they played it on sight and the second pass through they recorded it. And then because we were double tracking they played it a couple of times. I’m listening and I says, “God, that sounds great.” So understanding that there was a song that Peggy Lee recorded, I don't know if you remember, it was “Is That All There Is?”
And I left the studio and I said, “That wasn’t hard, it was really a lot of fun.”
